step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 21-year-old male Guinean national presenting with fever, vomiting, and diarrhea, imported to Senegal

step5_concept_grounding: Ebola virus disease caused by Zaire ebolavirus confirmed by Dakar Pasteur Institute

evidence_items.source_quote: On August 28, the test operated on the blood sample by the Dakar Pasteur Institute returned as Zaire-Ebola-virus-positive.

Three days after his arrival, he started showing signs of fever, vomiting and diarrhea with no bleeding, and then decided to consult in a suburban health centre where he had been taken in charge for three days.
evidence_items.test_name: Clinical presentation of acute febrile illness

rationale: A 21-year-old male traveled from Guinea to Senegal and presented with fever, vomiting, and diarrhea. Blood testing performed at the Dakar Pasteur Institute confirmed Zaire ebolavirus infection (E1 confirmatory evidence). The assertion is CONFIRMED_PRESENT, temporality CURRENT_EPISODE, clinical role PRIMARY_DIAGNOSIS. VPD criteria are fully satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 30-year-old woman presenting with acute Ebola virus disease complicated by late-onset encephalitis and polyarthritis

step5_concept_grounding: Ebola virus disease (EBOV) complicated by late-onset encephalitis and polyarthritis

evidence_items.source_quote: On day 8 of illness, after testing EBOV PCR-positive (cycle threshold [Ct] value of 23.5), she was given intravenous ceftriaxone (2 g) for 7 days, artesunate (180 mg) for 3 days, and Ringer's lactate (4-6 L) with supplemental KCl for 5 days.
cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was EBOV PCR-positive (Ct value 37.6), as determined by using the Public Health England in-house, optimized version of the Trombley assay with a cutoff Ct value of 40.

rationale: A 30-year-old female in Sierra Leone was diagnosed with acute Ebola virus disease confirmed by plasma RT-PCR (Ct 23.5). Following initial improvement, she developed late-onset encephalopathy with EBOV PCR positivity in cerebrospinal fluid (Ct 37.6) and subsequent intermittent PCR positivity in urine. E1 confirmatory laboratory evidence is present for the primary human patient in the current active episode. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: A 40-year-old Liberian male traveler who collapsed in Lagos, Nigeria with acute hemorrhagic fever

step5_concept_grounding: Zaire ebolavirus disease confirmed by RT-PCR and L-gene sequencing

evidence_items.source_quote: Investigations carried out on viral RNA purified from the blood and urine specimens of the patient revealed the presence of the expected amplicon size (300 bp) for Filoviruses (Figure 2).

The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (L) gene, partial Coding sequence (CDS) for EBOV/Hsap/NGA/2014/LIB-NIG 01072014 was deposited in the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) with the accession number KM251803.1.
evidence_items.test_name: L-gene Sanger sequencing and phylogenetic analysis

rationale: A 40-year-old Liberian male traveler arrived in Lagos, Nigeria and presented with high fever, sore throat, vomiting, diarrhea, and hematuria. RT-PCR on blood and urine specimens amplified the expected 300 bp filovirus product, and Sanger sequencing of the L-gene confirmed Zaire ebolavirus (GenBank KM251803.1). Confirmatory E1 molecular laboratory evidence is documented in the current active episode for the primary human patient. VPD satisfied -> POSITIVE.
